body.translated_text:
| <s>Śrīḥ</s> |
The <s>Śabdavyāpāravicāra</s> (Investigation of the Functions of Words) composed by the revered <s>Rājānaka Mammaṭācārya</s>.

body.text: iha heyopādeyānāṃ hānopādāne pramāṇād eva | tac ca niścayātmatayā prāmānyaṃ bhajate | niścayaś ca śabdasāhityenārthaṃ viṣayīkaroti | śabdasya cārthapratītipratipattilakṣaṇakāryānyathānupapattyā kārakatvāt kalpyamāno vyāparo 'bhidhādiśabdapratipādyo nānāprakāra iti tatparīkṣārthaṃ śabdavyāpāravicārātmakaṃ prakaraṇam idam ārabhyate | vyāpāraś ca śṛṅgagrāhikayā darśayituṃ na yujyate iti viṣayamukhena pradarśyate --

children.text: jātiḥ kriyā guṇaḥ saṃjñā vācyo 'rthaḥ samitadhvaniḥ |
children.translated_text: Universal (<s>jāti</s>), action (<s>kriyā</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), [and] proper name (<s>saṃjñā</s>)—[these are the grounds of] the expressible meaning; the [word whose] sound is conventionally associated [with these is the expresser].

children.text: agṛhītasaṅketasya śabdasyārthapratipatter abhāvāt saṅketasahāya eva śabdo 'rthaṃ pratipādayati | tena samitaḥ saṅketito dhvaniḥ śabdo yatra yo 'rthaḥ | pūrvam upalabhyatvān na tu viśrāntidhāmatvān mukhya iti prasiddho vācyo 'bhidheyo 'rthaḥ | tathā cāha -- jātir ityādi | iha yadyapi pravṛttinivṛttiviṣayo vyaktir eva, tathāpy ānantyad vyabhicārāc ca tatra saṅketaḥ kartum na pāryata iti gauḥ śuklaś calo ḍittha ityādīnām ekārthatvaṃ mā prasāṅkṣīd iti ca śabdānām upādhāv eva saṅketaḥ | upādhiś ca vastudharmo vaktṛyadṛcchāsaṃniveśitaś ca | ādyaḥ siddhaḥ sādhyaś ca | siddho 'pi dvividhaḥ padārthasya prāṇaprado viśeṣādhānahetuś ca | ādyo jātiḥ | uktaṃ hi vākyapadīye -- "gaur hi svarūpeṇa na gauḥ, nāpy agauḥ, gotvābhisaṃbandhāt tu gauḥ" iti | dvitīyo guṇaḥ | śuklādinā hi labdhasattākaṃ vastu viśeṣyate | sādhyaḥ pūrvāparībhūtāvayavaḥ kriyārūpaḥ | ḍitthādiśabdānāṃ antyabuddhinirgrāhyaṃ saṃhṛtakramaṃ svarūpaṃ vaktrā yadṛcchayā ḍitthādiṣv artheṣūpādhitayā saṃniveśyate iti ca saṃjñārūpo yadṛcchātmaka iti | gauḥ śuklaś calo ḍittha ityādau catuṣṭayī śabdānāṃ pravṛttir bhāṣye kathitā | paramāṇutvādīnāṃ tu guṇamadhyapāṭhāt pāribhāṣikaṃ guṇatvam | nanu payaḥśaṅkhādyāśrayībhūteṣu śuklādiguṇeṣu yadvaśena śuklaḥ śukla ity abhinnāv abhidhānapratyayau stas tacchuklatvādisāmānyam | guḍataṇḍulādipākeṣu evam eva pākatvādikam | śukasārikādyudīriteṣu ḍitthādiśabdeṣu ca ḍitthādiśabdatvaṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ bhidyamāne vā ḍitthādyarthe ḍitthāditvam astīti katham catuṣṭayī śabdānāṃ pravṛttiḥ | ucyate | saṃsthānāvasthānapramāṇavarṇair bhede 'pi vyaktīnāṃ śābaleyo gauḥ dhāvaleyo gaur ityādyekapratyayahetutvaṃ jāter eva | haṃsahārādīnāṃ ghṛtaguḍādīnāṃ śukasārikādyudīritaḍitthādiśabdānāṃ nānāvasthaḍitthādyarthānāṃ ca bhede 'pi haṃsaḥ śuklaḥ, hāraḥ śuklaḥ, ghṛtaṃ pacyate, guḍaṃ pacyate, ḍitthaśabdo ḍitthaśabdaḥ, ḍittho ḍittha ityekākārāvagatinibandhanatvād ekarūpatvam eva guṇakriyāyadṛcchānām iti naitāsāṃ bhinneṣv abhinnābhidhānapratyayahetur jātir ghaṭata iti catvāry eva śabdapravṛttinimittāni ||
children.translated_text: Since there is no cognition of meaning from a word whose convention (<s>saṅketa</s>) has not been grasped, a word communicates meaning only with the aid of convention. Therefore, the meaning (<s>artha</s>) of that word (<s>dhvani</s>, sound) which is conventionally associated (<s>samita</s>, i.e., <s>saṅketita</s>) [with it is its expressible meaning]. Because it is apprehended first—not because it is the resting-place [of cognition]—[this meaning] is the primary (<s>mukhya</s>), well-known, expressible (<s>vācya</s>), denotable (<s>abhidheya</s>) meaning. And so he says: "universal (<s>jāti</s>)" and so forth. Here, although the object of engagement and disengagement is the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) alone, nevertheless, because of its infinity and because of the deviation [that would result], convention cannot be established with respect to it. And lest there arise a conflation of meaning in expressions like "cow," "white," "moving," "<s>Ḍittha</s>," etc., convention is established only with respect to the imposed property (<s>upādhi</s>). The imposed property is either a real property of a thing (<s>vastudharma</s>) or one arbitrarily assigned by the speaker (<s>vaktṛyadṛcchā</s>). The first is either established (<s>siddha</s>) or to-be-accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>). The established, too, is of two kinds: that which bestows existence on the referent (<s>padārtha</s>), and that which is the cause of particularization. The first is the universal (<s>jāti</s>). For it has been said in the <s>Vākyapadīya</s>: "A cow is not a cow by its own form, nor is it a non-cow; it is a cow by virtue of its connection with cowness (<s>gotva</s>)." The second is quality (<s>guṇa</s>). For a thing that has already attained existence is particularized by whiteness and so forth. The to-be-accomplished [property], having parts that are sequentially ordered, takes the form of action (<s>kriyā</s>). As for words like "<s>Ḍittha</s>," their own form—compressed in sequence and grasped by the final cognition—is arbitrarily assigned by the speaker as an imposed property upon objects such as <s>Ḍittha</s> and so on; this is the proper-name type (<s>saṃjñā</s>), which is arbitrary (<s>yadṛcchātmaka</s>) in nature. In [the <s>Mahābhāṣya</s> commentary on] expressions like "cow," "white," "moving," "<s>Ḍittha</s>," a fourfold basis of word-application has been stated. As for [properties such as] atomicity (<s>paramāṇutva</s>) and the like, their being listed among qualities is a technical (<s>pāribhāṣika</s>) classification. [Objection:] Now, with respect to the qualities of whiteness and so forth residing in substrates such as milk, conch-shell, etc.—the universal of whiteness (<s>śuklatvasāmānya</s>) is that by virtue of which there are identical expression and cognition [in the utterances] "white, white." Similarly, with respect to the cooking of treacle, rice, etc., there is the universal of cooking (<s>pākatva</s>). And with respect to words like "<s>Ḍittha</s>" uttered by parrots, <s>mynah</s> birds, etc., there is <s>Ḍittha</s>-word-ness; and with respect to the object <s>Ḍittha</s> that changes from moment to moment, there is <s>Ḍittha</s>-ness—so how can there be a [merely] fourfold basis of word-application? [Reply:] It is said: Even though individuals differ in shape, condition, size, and color, it is the universal (<s>jāti</s>) alone that is the cause of a single cognition, as in "the dappled one is a cow," "the white one is a cow," etc. But for swans and garlands, for ghee and treacle, for the word "<s>Ḍittha</s>" uttered by parrots and <s>mynah</s> birds, and for the object <s>Ḍittha</s> in its various states—even though they differ—since the basis of a uniform cognition, such as "the swan is white, the garland is white," "ghee is cooked, treacle is cooked," "the <s>Ḍittha</s>-word is a <s>Ḍittha</s>-word," "<s>Ḍittha</s> is <s>Ḍittha</s>," is precisely their uniformity of form, therefore quality, action, and arbitrary name do indeed possess a single form. Hence, the universal (<s>jāti</s>)—which would be the cause of identical expression and cognition among different [instances]—does not apply to these, and so the grounds of word-application are exactly four.

body.translated_text: Here, the abandonment and adoption of what is to be abandoned and adopted [respectively] proceeds from <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) alone. And that [cognition] assumes its validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) by virtue of being a determinate cognition (<s>niścaya</s>). Determinate cognition, moreover, takes its object in conjunction with words. And since the function (<s>vyāpāra</s>) of a word—postulated through the impossibility of otherwise explaining its effect, namely the cognition and communication of meaning—is of various kinds, designated by terms such as <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) and so forth, this treatise (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), whose subject is the investigation of word-functions (<s>śabdavyāpāravicāra</s>), is commenced for the purpose of examining them. And since the function [of words] cannot be demonstrated in an exhaustive manner, it is demonstrated through the subject matter [itself]—

children.translated_text: When that [primary meaning] is obstructed, [the word denotes] a meaning to be indicated (<s>lakṣya</s>) through indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), either from convention (<s>rūḍhi</s>) or from [connection with] the [primary] meaning, [a meaning] connected with that [primary meaning]. || 1 ||

children.text: śabde kuśala ityādau darbhagrahaṇādyayogāt gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityādau ca gaṅgādīnāṃ ca ghoṣādhikaraṇatāsaṃbhavāt mukhyārthasya bādhaḥ, rūḍitaḥ prasiddheḥ tathā gaṅgātaṭa ityāder yeṣāṃ na tathā pratipattis teṣāṃ pāvanatvādīnāṃ tathāpratipādanātmanā prayojanena | tena mukhyenārthenānvito lakṣaṇīyo lakṣaṇāvyāpāragocaraḥ | saṃbandhaś cātra vivekatvādiḥ sāmīpyādiś ca | evaṃ vācyavācakārthaniṣṭhau vyāpārāv abhidhālakṣaṇe |
children.translated_text: In expressions like "<s>śabde kuśalaḥ</s>" ("skilled in words"), there is an obstruction of the primary meaning (<s>mukhyārtha-bādha</s>) because there is no connection with the act of grasping <s>darbha</s> grass [which is the primary meaning of <s>kuśala</s>]; and in expressions like "<s>Gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>" ("the hamlet is on the Gaṅgā"), because it is impossible for the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and such [rivers] to be the locus of a hamlet. [This obstruction occurs] through <s>rūḍhi</s> (conventional usage), through established understanding, such as "<s>Gaṅgā-taṭa</s>" (bank of the Gaṅgā) and the like; for those who do not have such an understanding directly, through a purpose consisting in the communication of qualities such as sanctity and the like. Through such [obstruction], what is to be indicated (<s>lakṣaṇīya</s>) — the object of the operation of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (secondary signification) — is connected with the primary meaning. And the relation here is one of distinctiveness (<s>vivekatva</s>) etc., or proximity (<s>sāmīpya</s>) etc. Thus, the two operations — <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) — are established in the relation between the expressed (<s>vācya</s>) and the expressor (<s>vācaka</s>).
The drawing in of another for one's own accomplishment, and the offering up of oneself for the sake of another —

children.text: upādānaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cety uktā śuddhaiva sā dvividhā || 2 ||
children.translated_text: these are called <s>upādāna</s> (adoption) and <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (indication); and that [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] when unmixed is said to be of two kinds. // 2 //

children.text: kuntān praveśaya yaṣṭī praveśayetyādau kuntādibhir ātmanaḥ praveśasiddhaye svasaṃyoginaḥ puruṣā ākṣipyante | tata upādāneneyaṃ lakṣaṇā | "gaur anubandhyaḥ" ityādau śruticoditam anubandhanaṃ kathaṃ me syād iti jātyā vyaktir ākṣipyate na tu śabdenocyate | "viśeṣyaṃ nābhidhā gacchet kṣiṇaśaktir viśeṣaṇe" iti nyāyād upādānalakṣaṇā nodāhartavyā | na hy atra prayojanam asti na vā rūḍhiḥ | vyaktyavinābhāvāt tu jātyā vyaktir ākṣipyate yathā kriyatām ity atra kartā, kurv ity atra karma, praviśa piṇḍīm ityādau gṛhaṃ bhakṣayetyādi ca | pīno devadatto divā na bhuṅkte ity atra ca rātribhojanaṃ na lakṣyate | śrutārthāpatter arthāpatter vā tasya viṣayatvāt | gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ity atra taṭasya ghoṣādhikaraṇatāyāḥ siddhaye gaṅgāśabdaḥ svārtham arpayatīty evamādau lakṣaṇenaiṣā lakṣaṇā | ubhayarūpā ceyaṃ śuddhā upacāreṇāmiśritvāt | anayor bhedayor lakṣyasya lakṣakasya ca na bhedarūpaṃ taṭasthatvam | taṭādīnāṃ gaṅgādiśabdaiḥ pratipādane tattvapratipattau hi pratipipādayiṣitaprayojanasampratyayaḥ | gaṅgāsambandhamātrapratītau tu gaṅgātaṭe ghoṣa iti mukhyaśabdābhidhānāl lakṣaṇāyāḥ ko bhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In expressions like "bring in the lances" (<s>kuntān praveśaya</s>) [meaning] "bring in the spear-bearers," through the lances and such [words], for the accomplishment of their own entry, the persons connected with them are drawn in. Hence this <s>lakṣaṇā</s> operates through <s>upādāna</s> (adoption). In [the Vedic injunction] "<s>gaur anubandhyaḥ</s>" ("the cow is to be tied as a sacrificial animal"), the individual [animal] is drawn in by the class (<s>jāti</s>) for the purpose of [fulfilling] the tying enjoined by scripture — "how shall the tying be accomplished for me?" — but is not stated by the word itself. According to the principle that "the denotative power, being exhausted in the qualifier, does not reach the qualified" (<s>viśeṣyaṃ nābhidhā gacchet kṣīṇaśaktir viśeṣaṇe</s>), <s>upādāna-lakṣaṇā</s> should not be illustrated [here], for there is neither a purpose nor a convention [to obstruct the primary meaning]. But because the individual is inseparable from the class, the individual is drawn in by the class — just as in "let it be done" the agent [is implied], in "do" the object [is implied], and in "enter the hall" the meaning "eat food" [is implied], etc. In "fat <s>Devadatta</s> does not eat during the day," eating at night is not indicated [by <s>lakṣaṇā</s>], because that is the domain of <s>śrutārthāpatti</s> (verbal presumption) or <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). In "the hamlet is on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>" (<s>Gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>), the word <s>Gaṅgā</s> offers up its own meaning for the accomplishment of the bank's being the locus of the hamlet — in such cases, this <s>lakṣaṇā</s> operates through <s>lakṣaṇa</s> (indication). And this [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] in both forms is unmixed (<s>śuddhā</s>), not being combined with figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>). In these two varieties, there is no distinct difference between the indicated (<s>lakṣya</s>) and the indicator (<s>lakṣaka</s>), as that would be a mere external distinction. For when the bank and such [entities] are denoted by words like <s>Gaṅgā</s>, understanding of the true referent involves the comprehension of the intended purpose. But if only the mere relation with <s>Gaṅgā</s> were understood, what would be the difference from the primary denotation "the hamlet on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>"?

children.text: sāropānyā tu yatroktau viṣayī viṣayas tathā |
children.translated_text: The other [type] is <s>sāropā</s> (with superimposition), where the superimposed and the substrate are stated [together],

children.text: āropyamāṇa āropaviśayaś ca yatrānupahnutabhedau sāmānādhikaraṇyena nirdiśyete sā lakṣaṇā sāropā |
children.translated_text: Where the superimposed entity and the substrate of superimposition are expressed in co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) without concealing the distinction [between them] — that <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is called <s>sāropā</s> (with superimposition).
When another [i.e., the substrate] is absorbed within the superimposed [entity], that [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] becomes <s>sādhyavasānikā</s> (conclusive). // 3 //

When the other, the substrate of superimposition, is absorbed (<s>antaḥkṛta</s>), that is, swallowed up (<s>nigīrṇa</s>), by the superimposed entity (<s>āropyamāṇa-viṣayin</s>) — that is <s>sādhyavasānā</s> (conclusive <s>lakṣaṇā</s>).

children.text: bhedāv imau ca sādṛśyāt saṃbandhāntaratas tathā |
children.translated_text: And these two varieties [are to be understood as arising] from similarity, and also from other relations,
as figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>) and as unmixed (<s>śuddha</s>) — thus they should be known.

children.text:
imāv āropādhyavasānarūpau sādṛśyahetū gaur vāhīka ity atra gaur ayam ity atra ca | atra svārthasahacāriṇo guṇā jāḍyamāndyādayo lakṣyamāṇā api gośabdasya parārthābhidhānaṃ prati nimittatvam upayāntīti kecit | svārthasahacāriguṇābhedena parārthagatā guṇā eva lakṣyante na tu parārtho 'bhidhīyata ity apare | sādhāraṇaguṇāśrayaṇena parārtha eva lakṣyata ity anye | uktaṃ cānyatra --
  abhidheyāvinābhūtapratītir lakṣaṇocyate |
  lakṣyamāṇaguṇair yogād vṛtter iṣṭā tu gauṇatā
iti | avinābhāvo 'tra sambandhamātraṃ na tu nāntarīyakatvam | tattve hi mañcāḥ krośantītyādau lakṣaṇā na syāt | avinābhāve cākṣepeṇaiva siddher lakṣaṇāyā nopayoga ity uktam | yena gogatajāḍyamāndyādisadṛśajāḍyamāndyetyādy ucyate tena guṇābhedābhyupagame guṇajātiprasaṅgāc catuṣṭayī śabdānāṃ pravṛttir uktā vyāhanyate |
  āyur ghṛtam, āyur evedam ityādau sādṛśyād anyaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvādiḥ paraḥ sambandhaḥ | evamādau ca kāryakāraṇabhāvādilakṣaṇapūrve āropādhyavasāne | atra gauṇabhedayor bhede 'pi tādrūpyapratītiḥ sarvathāivābhedāvagamaś ca prayojanam | śuddhabhedayos tv anyavailakṣaṇyenāvyabhicāreṇa ca kāryakāritvādi | kvacit tādarthyād upacāraḥ, yathā indrārthā sthūṇā indraḥ | kvacit svasvāmibhāvāt, yathā rājakīyaḥ puruṣo rājā | kvacid avayavāvayavibhāvāt, yathā agrahasta ity atrāgramātrāvayave hastaḥ | kvacit tātkarmyāt, yathā atakṣā takṣā |
children.translated_text:
These two—superimposition (<s>āropa</s>) and determination (<s>adhyavasāna</s>)—are based on similarity (<s>sādṛśya</s>), as in "a cow" [said of] a Bāhīka [person, meaning he is stupid like a cow], and in "this is a cow" [said of something that is not actually a cow]. Here, some hold that the qualities co-occurring with the primary meaning—such as stupidity, dullness, etc.—even though they are indicated (<s>lakṣyamāṇa</s>), serve as the ground for the cow-word's denoting the secondary meaning. Others hold that it is precisely the qualities belonging to the secondary referent, being non-different from the qualities co-occurring with the primary referent, that are indicated—but the secondary referent itself is not denoted. Still others hold that the secondary referent itself is indicated through recourse to the shared qualities. And it has been stated elsewhere: "The cognition [of a meaning] inseparable from the denotable meaning is called <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication); but when the usage is based on conjunction with the qualities being indicated, it is preferred [to call it] <s>gauṇatā</s> (figurative usage)." Here, 'inseparability' (<s>avinābhāva</s>) means merely a relation, not strict logical entailment; for otherwise, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> would not apply in cases like "the platforms are shouting" [where the people on the platforms are meant]. And [it has been] said that when the inseparability can be established through implication (<s>ākṣepa</s>) alone, there is no need for <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. By those who speak of similarity of stupidity, dullness, etc. to the stupidity, dullness, etc. belonging to cows—if non-difference of qualities is accepted, then, since the absurd consequence of a universal of qualities would follow, the fourfold basis of word-application stated [earlier] would be contradicted.
In [expressions such as] "Ghee is life" (<s>āyur ghṛtam</s>), "This is life itself," etc., besides similarity, there is another relation—namely cause-and-effect and the like. And in such cases, superimposition and determination are preceded by indication based on cause-and-effect, etc. Here, although figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>) and indicative (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) usages differ, the purpose [of the former] is the cognition of likeness (<s>tādrūpya</s>), while [the purpose of the latter] is the comprehension of complete non-difference. For the two that are purely indicative [i.e., non-figurative <s>lakṣaṇā</s>], however, [the purpose is] causal efficacy and the like, through distinction from others and non-deviation. In some cases, the figurative transfer (<s>upacāra</s>) is due to being-for-the-sake-of (<s>tādarthya</s>), as [when] a pillar [erected] for <s>Indra</s> [is called] "<s>Indra</s>." In some cases, it is due to the master-servant relation (<s>svasvāmibhāva</s>), as [when] a royal servant is [called] "the king." In some cases, it is due to the part-whole relation (<s>avayavāvayavibhāva</s>), as in "tip-hand" (<s>agrahasta</s>), where "hand" [is used for] the mere tip as a part. In some cases, it is due to performing the action of (<s>tātkarmya</s>), as [when] a non-carpenter is [called] a "carpenter" (<s>takṣā</s>).
<s>Lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) is thus sixfold. || 4 ||

children.text:
ādyabhedābhyāṃ saha |
  sā ca "vaktur vākyasya vācyasya rūpabhedād vibhidyate" | tatra vaktṛsvarūpaparyālocanāt sā yathā --
children.translated_text: Together with the first two divisions [i.e., <s>rūḍhi</s> and <s>artha</s>-based]. And this [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] "varies according to differences in the form of the speaker, the sentence, and the expressible meaning." Among these, [here is an example] arising from consideration of the speaker's nature—

children.text: upakṛtaṃ bahu tatra kim ucyate sujanatā prathitā bhavatā param |
children.translated_text: "Much has been done [by you]; what more can be said? Your goodness, sir, has become widely renowned.

children.text: vidadhad īdṛśam eva sadā sakhe sukhitam āssva tataḥ śaradām śatam ||
children.translated_text: Doing always just so, O friend, may you live happily for a hundred autumns."

body.text:
bahubhir upakārais tāpyamānasya kasyacid uktir iyam | ato vaktṛmahimnā mūrkhe bṛhaspatiḍśabdena mūrkhatvam ivāpakāriṇi durjanatvādy atra lakṣyate |
  vākyaviśeṣāvadhāraṇād yathā --

children.translated_text: "Blessed are you, who can recount even in the intimacy of love
hundreds of confident endearments whispered between bouts of passion;

children.text: nīvīṃ prati praṇihite ca kare priyeṇa
children.translated_text: and when your beloved's hand reaches toward your garment-knot—

children.text: sakhyaḥ śapāmi yadi kiṃcid api smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: I swear, dear friend, I do not remember even the slightest thing!"

body.translated_text:
This is the utterance of someone tormented by another's many [supposed] favors. Therefore, by the greatness [i.e., the ironic character] of the speaker, [when the word] "<s>Bṛhaspati</s>" [is used of] a fool, what is indicated is foolishness; [similarly,] in the case of a malefactor [called "good person"], wickedness and the like are indicated here.
An example arising from ascertainment of a particular sentence—

body.text:
atra dhanyāsmi lakṣyate | vākyasyaivātra śaktiḥ |
  vācyaviśeṣanirūpaṇād yathā --

children.translated_text: "Of you whose power is devoted to granting fearlessness to the world,
whose wealth is being wholly appropriated [by others]—
the fault of mounting the same yoke [i.e., rivaling you],
O wise one, no one at any time is able to commit."

body.translated_text:
Here, "I am blessed" is the indicated meaning. It is the sentence itself that has the power [to convey this ironic sense].
An example arising from examination of the particular expressible meaning—

body.text: atra prāṇasamasya vyasane 'pi taṭasthas tṛṇamātram api dātum asamarthaś ca vācyaḥ | evaṃ dvikabhedās trayaḥ trikabhedaś caika udāhāryaḥ |

children.text: dṛṣṭiṃ he prativeśini kṣaṇam ihāpy asmadgṛhe dāsyasi
children.translated_text: "O neighbor-woman, will you cast your gaze even for a moment upon my house?

children.text: prāyo naiva śiśoḥ pitāsya virasāḥ kaupīr apaḥ pāsyasi |
children.translated_text: Perhaps you will not drink the insipid gruel-water of this child's father.

children.text: ekākiny api yāmi tad drutam itaḥ srotas tamālākulaṃ
children.translated_text: Alone I go—swiftly, then, from here to the river-bank dense with <s>tamāla</s> trees;
let the hard, jointless knots of old reeds scratch my body without a gap."

body.translated_text: Here, the expressible meaning is: [he is] one who, even when his dearest friend is in calamity, stands apart as a bystander and is incapable of giving even a blade of grass. Thus, examples of two-part divisions are three, and the example of the three-part division is one [more]—

children.text: prāptaśrīr eṣa kasmāt punar api mayi taṃ manthakhedaṃ vidadhyān
children.translated_text: "Why should he who has already attained <s>Śrī</s> (Prosperity/Lakṣmī) inflict upon me again that toil of churning?

children.text: nidrām apy asya pūrvām analasamanaso naiva sambhāvayāmi |
children.translated_text: I cannot even imagine that his former sleep [upon <s>Śeṣa</s>] could return, he whose mind is [now restless] like fire.

children.text: setuṃ badhnāti bhūyaḥ kim iti ca sakaladvīpanāthānuyāte
children.translated_text: 'Why does he build a bridge again?'—thus, at your approach,

children.text: tvayy āyāte vitarkān iti dadhata ivābhāti kampaḥ payodheḥ ||
children.translated_text: O you who are attended by all the lords of the islands—the trembling of the ocean seems as if it harbors such anxious thoughts."

children.text: durvārā madaneṣavo diśi diśi vyājṛmbhate mādhavo
children.translated_text: "The arrows of <s>Madana</s> (the Love-god) are irresistible; in every direction <s>Mādhava</s> (Spring) displays its splendor;
the moonbeams cause madness in the heart, and the <s>kokilas</s> (cuckoo birds) steal the mind.
This body, difficult to bear with the weight of high breasts—and then that other couple [of torments];

children.text: soḍhavyāḥ sakhi sāmprataṃ katham amī pañcāgnayo duḥsahā ||
children.translated_text: how, O friend, are these five unbearable fires to be endured now?"

body.text:
ity atra ca nādeyapānīyānayanena parapuruṣasambhogasya naḍagranthalekhanena sambhāvyamānanakhadaśanakṣatānāṃ ca nihnavātmakaṃ vastu, bhavān harir iti rūpakālaṃkāraḥ, vipralambhaśṛṅgāraś ca raso lakṣyata iti nodāhāryam | mukhyārthasya bādhābhāvāt | asakhyā api sakhyabhidhānasyaivaṃ sambhavāt | ākṣiptasyālaṅkārasya lakṣyatve ca vahnyānayane pātrānayanasya lakṣyatvaprasaṅgāt | abādhitasyaiva vācyasya rasapratītikṛttvāt | saprayojanāyāṃ ca lakṣaṇāyāṃ tadatirikto vyāpāro 'vaśyam aṅgīkartavyaḥ | tathā ca sati prayojane lakṣaṇā | tac ca na mukhyārthabādhanimittavat pramāṇāntarād boddhavyam | tadartham eva lakṣaṇāśabdaprayogāt | na khalu śābde 'rthe pratyakṣaṃ kramate | nāpi tatpūrvakam anumānam | nānumānāntaram anavasthāpatteḥ | na smṛtiḥ tadanubhavābhāvāt | satyām api vā tasyāṃ niyatasmaraṇaṃ na syāt | tasmāc chabda eva tatra pramāṇam | nirvyāpāraś ca śabdo nārthapratītikṛt | vyāpāraś ca nābhidhā tatra saṅketābhāvāt | na lakṣaṇā tasmin sati hi sā na tu tadviṣayā | nāpy asyā lakṣye bādho 'sti | lakṣyaprayojanayoś ca sambandhasya prayojanasya cābhāvāt | tasyāpi lakṣaṇe 'navasthāpattir iti na lakṣaṇā syāt | asti ca sā | tataḥ prayojanaviṣayo vyāpārao 'bhyupagantavyaḥ | sa ca dhvananāvagamanaprakāśanadyotanādiśabdavyavahāryaḥ |
  nanu gaṅgātaṭe ghoṣa ityādisvaśabdād yādṛgarthapratītir na bhavati tādṛśī gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa ityādes tad eva prayojanaṃ pāvanatvādidharmākrāntaṃ ca taṭādi lakṣyate iti viśiśṭe lakṣaṇā na tu lakṣite viśeṣāḥ | evaṃ hi taṭādeḥ pāvanatvādīnāṃ ca dharmadharmibhāvaś caturtho vyāpāra urarīkartavyaḥ | lakṣaṇāphalaṃ ca katham anyena kriyate | na ca vyāpārasya lakṣaṇātmano vyañjanātmā vyāpāro bhavati | śabdasyāsāv iti cen na | tarhi lakṣaṇāyāḥ prayojanaṃ tasmād viśiṣṭam eva lakṣyate | ucyate | lakṣaṇāyās taṭādir viṣayaḥ | na ca tatra pāvanatvādayaḥ santi | tat kathaṃ viśiṣṭe lakṣaṇā | sāmānyaniṣṭhaś ca saṅketa iti tritayātmanā saṅketabhedena lakṣaṇā sā kathaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ gocarīkuryāt | vyajyate tv asaṅketita eva | kiṃca lakṣaṇāyā gocaro lakṣyo na prayojanam | pratyakṣasya hi nīlaṃ viṣayaḥ | prakaṭatā saṃvittir vā phalam | avyabhicārāc ca lakṣyasaṃvit phalatvenoktā | evaṃ hy abhidhāyā api phalaṃ śabdasya ca vācakasya saṃvid eva phalam | tac ca vinā vyāpārān na sambhavati | na ca vyāpārasya vyāpāra iti śabdasyaivāsau vācyaḥ | lakṣaṇānvayavyatirekānuvidhānaṃ ca savyāpārasya phalasyeti tasyās tat kāryaṃ kāryaṃ ca phalam ucyate | kriyāntaraprāpyasya yāgaphalatvam iva vyañjanaśaktinirvartyasya prayojanasya lakṣaṇāphalatvam | nīlaviṣayasya pramāṇasya yathā nīlaniṣṭhaiva prakaṭatā saṃvid vā phalam tadval lakṣaṇāyās tadviṣayaniṣṭham eva prayojanam | tena dharmadharmibhāvaparikalpakaṃ nopayujyate vyāpārāntaram | tena siddham etal lakṣaṇāyā atirikto vyāpāraḥ samāśraṇīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And here, the concealment (<s>nihnava</s>) of the liaison with another man through bringing river-water, and of the supposed nail-and-tooth-marks through writing with reed-pens—this is the content based on concealment. 'You are <s>Hari</s>' is the figure of speech <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). And the <s>rasa</s> of love-in-separation (<s>vipralambha-śṛṅgāra</s>) is perceived—thus [this] cannot be cited as an example [of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> alone]. Because there is no obstruction (<s>bādha</s>) of the primary meaning (<s>mukhyārtha</s>). Because even for a non-friend, such address as 'friend' (<s>sakhī</s>) is possible. And if the suggested (<s>ākṣipta</s>) figure of speech were taken as the <s>lakṣya</s> (indicated meaning), there would be the undesirable consequence that in 'bring fire,' the bringing of a pot would also be the <s>lakṣya</s>. Because it is the unobstructed expressible meaning (<s>vācya</s>) itself that produces the cognition of <s>rasa</s>. And when <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) has a purpose (<s>prayojana</s>), a function (<s>vyāpāra</s>) beyond it must necessarily be accepted. And thus, when there is a purpose, [there is] <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. And that [purpose] is not to be known from another <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), as in the case of the occasion of obstruction of primary meaning. Because the use of the word '<s>lakṣaṇā</s>' is precisely for that purpose. Indeed, perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) does not operate with regard to verbal meaning. Nor [does] inference (<s>anumāna</s>) based on that [perception]. Nor another inference, for that would lead to infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>). Nor memory (<s>smṛti</s>), due to the absence of prior experience of it. Or even if [memory] existed, there would be no certain recollection. Therefore, the word (<s>śabda</s>) itself is the <s>pramāṇa</s> there. And a word without function (<s>vyāpāra</s>) does not produce cognition of meaning. And the function there is not denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>), due to the absence of convention (<s>saṅketa</s>). Nor is it <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication); for when that [<s>lakṣya</s>] exists, that [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] exists, but it does not have that [purpose] as its object. Nor is there obstruction of this [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] in its <s>lakṣya</s>. And because of the absence of a connection between the <s>lakṣya</s> and the purpose, and of a [further] purpose [for it]. If that [purpose] too were [the object of] <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, there would be infinite regress; therefore it would not be <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. And yet that [function] exists. Therefore, a function whose object is the purpose must be accepted. And it is designated by the words <s>dhvanana</s> (suggesting), <s>avagamana</s> (comprehending), <s>prakāśana</s> (illuminating), <s>dyotana</s> (manifesting), etc. [Objection:] Now, from the proper expression '<s>gaṅgātaṭe ghoṣaḥ</s>' ('the village is on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>') etc., such cognition as does not arise—[but] such [extra cognition does arise] from '<s>gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>' ('the village is on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>') etc. That very purpose, namely the bank etc. pervaded by properties like sanctity (<s>pāvanatva</s>), is what is indicated—so there is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> of the qualified meaning (<s>viśiṣṭa</s>), not [separate] qualifiers of the indicated meaning. [Reply:] For in that case, the <s>dharma-dharmin</s> (property-property-bearer) relation of the bank etc. with sanctity etc. would require acceptance of a fourth function. And how can the result (<s>phala</s>) of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> be accomplished by another [function]? And a function of <s>vyañjanā</s> nature cannot belong to a function of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> nature. If [you say] it belongs to the word [itself]—no; then the purpose [would be] of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, so only the qualified [meaning] is indicated. It is replied: The object (<s>viṣaya</s>) of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is the bank etc. And sanctity etc. do not exist there [by convention]. Then how can <s>lakṣaṇā</s> [target] the qualified [meaning]? And since convention (<s>saṅketa</s>) rests on the universal, how can that <s>lakṣaṇā</s>—through a threefold differentiation of convention—have the qualified as its domain? Rather, the unconventionalized [meaning] is suggested (<s>vyajyate</s>). Moreover, the domain of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is the <s>lakṣya</s>, not the purpose. For the object of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is 'blue'; its result is manifestation or awareness (<s>saṃvit</s>). And since <s>lakṣya</s>-awareness is spoken of as the result [of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>] due to invariable concomitance, so too is the result of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation)—the result of the word as expresser is awareness alone. And that is not possible without a function. And a function cannot have a [further] function—so it must be attributed to the word itself. And the conformity to the presence and absence of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> belongs to the result that is accompanied by a function—so that [result] is its effect, and effect is called result (<s>phala</s>). Just as the fruit of sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) is attainable through another action, so the purpose accomplished by the power of suggestion (<s>vyañjana-śakti</s>) is the result of <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. Just as the result of a <s>pramāṇa</s> whose object is 'blue' is the manifestation or awareness resting in that blue itself, so the purpose of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> rests in its own object alone. Therefore, no additional function that constructs the <s>dharma-dharmin</s> relation is needed. Thus it is established: a function additional to <s>lakṣaṇā</s> must be resorted to.

children.text: nirūḍhā kācanānyā tu kāryā sā kācid anyathā |
children.translated_text: Some [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>] is established (<s>nirūḍhā</s>); another, however, is to be effected (<s>kāryā</s>); and some [operates] otherwise.

children.text: anulomapratikūlādiśabdeṣu kācana sā vācyam arthaṃ parihṛtya lakṣya evārthe vācakavan nirūḍhā | aparā tu mukhyārthabādhanimittaprayojaneṣu satsu kartavyā |
children.translated_text: In words like '<s>anuloma</s>' (favorable), '<s>pratikūla</s>' (adverse), etc., some [<s>lakṣaṇā</s>], having set aside the expressible (<s>vācya</s>) meaning, is established (<s>nirūḍhā</s>) in just the <s>lakṣya</s> (indicated) meaning, functioning like a denotative word. Another, however, when the conditions of obstruction of primary meaning, purpose, and connection are present, is to be effected (<s>kāryā</s>).
Robbed of its beauty by the sun, with its orb covered by frost,
the moon does not shine, like a mirror dimmed by breath.

body.text: ityādāv andhādiśabdeṣu anupapadyamānatvād vācyam atyantatiraskṛtam iti vicchāyatvasya lakṣitasyāsāmānyatvaṃ vyaṅgyam | tathā --

children.text: sa puruṣaḥ sa ca jīvati satkṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: He [alone] is a man, and he truly lives, whose fame—honored
in the world, gathered through valor—
wanders this earth together with the sun's rays,
ever freshly arisen and blossoming.

body.translated_text: In [expressions] such as 'blind' (<s>andha</s>) and so forth, since [the primary meaning] is inapplicable, the expressible meaning (<s>vācya</s>) is completely excluded; thus the indicated quality of 'being devoid of luster' (<s>vicchāyatva</s>) is of an uncommon type—[and this] is the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>). Similarly—

body.text: ityādau puruṣaśabdo 'nupayujyamānatvāl lakṣitasvagataparākramavattvādidharmavyaṅgyatadānantyasaṅkramitavācyaḥ | rephadvayānugatabhramarādiśabdābhidheyatve dvirephaśabdaḥ ṣaṭpade yathā prayujyate tathā kokilādau dvika ityādikā anyathā na prayojyāḥ |

children.translated_text: And when the connection [of meanings] has been stated, that [indication comes] afterwards.

children.text: ihānantyād vyabhicārāc ca vākyasya vākyārtha iva viśeṣarūpe padārthe padasya saṅketaḥ kartuṃ na pāryate iti sāmānya eva saṅketaḥ | ākāṅkṣāsannidhiyogyatāvaśāt sāmānyānām abhihitānāṃ satām anvaya iti padārthānāṃ vaiśiṣṭyam | evaṃ cāpadārtho 'pi vākyārthas tātparyaśaktyā pratipādyate | atra pakṣe pūrvam abhidhā tato 'nvayabādhe lakṣaṇā |
children.translated_text: Here, due to [the] infinity [of particulars] and due to deviation, just as convention (<s>saṅketa</s>) of a sentence with respect to a particular sentence-meaning cannot be established, so too convention of a word with respect to a particular word-meaning cannot be established; hence convention is with respect to the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) alone. Through the force of expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), proximity (<s>sannidhi</s>), and compatibility (<s>yogyatā</s>), the connection (<s>anvaya</s>) of the universals that have been expressed—this [yields] the particularity of word-meanings. And thus even what is not a word-meaning [directly]—namely, the sentence-meaning (<s>vākyārtha</s>)—is communicated by the power of purport (<s>tātparyaśakti</s>). In this view, first there is denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>), then upon obstruction of [direct] connection, indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>).
In the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (expression-of-the-connected) [view], on the other hand, [indication comes] first. || 5 ||

children.text: devadatta gām ānayetyady uttamavṛddhavākyaśravaṇān madhyamavṛddhau viśiṣṭaṃ vyāpāraṃ karotīti dṛṣṭvā vyutpādyamāno nirvibhāge 'rthe nirvibhāgaṃ vākyaṃ vācakaṃ jānāti | tato yajñadatta gām ānayetyādivākyāntaraprayoge sati anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ niyatasya niyatārtham avasyatīti sāmānyāvacchādite viśiṣṭa eva padārthe padānāṃ saṅketa ity anvitānām eva satām abhidhānam iti viśiṣṭānāṃ padārthatā | atra pakṣe abhidhāyāḥ pura ādau lakṣaṇā, viśiṣṭasyaiva padārthatvāt |
children.translated_text: Upon hearing an excellent, well-formed sentence such as '<s>Devadatta</s>, bring the cow,' observing that a person of mature understanding performs a specific action, one being instructed [initially] understands the undivided sentence as the expresser of an undivided meaning. Then, when another sentence such as '<s>Yajñadatta</s>, bring the cow' is employed, through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvayavyatireka</s>), one determines the fixed [word] as having a fixed meaning—thus convention (<s>saṅketa</s>) pertains to the particular word-meaning as delimited by the universal; [this means that] the expression is of [meanings as] already connected (<s>anvita</s>)—[and this constitutes] the particularity of word-meanings. In this view, indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) comes first, at the outset, before denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>), since only the qualified [meaning] (<s>viśiṣṭa</s>) is the word-meaning.
In both [views], both [are present].

children.text: padāpekṣayābhihitānvayaḥ vākyāpekṣayā tv anvitābhidhānam iti dvayapakṣe dvayam | abhidhāyāḥ paścāt purastāc ca sā |
children.translated_text: From the standpoint of the word, [the view is] <s>abhihitānvaya</s> (connection of what has been expressed); from the standpoint of the sentence, <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (expression of the connected)—thus in the pair of views there is a pair [of positions]. Indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) comes both after and before denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>).
But in [the view of] an undivided sentence-meaning (<s>akhaṇḍa vākyārtha</s>), [indication] does not truly exist.

children.text:
vākyam eva vākyārthasya vācakam | padeṣu varṇavad vākyeṣu hi padānām anarthakatvam | tataś ca lakṣaṇā nāsty eva | kaśābhidhānāt turagasya yathā preṣito 'ham anena dhāvana iti pratibhodeti tadvat pratibhāvaśād viśiṣtavākyāt pratipattir iti saiva vākyārthaḥ | asatyabhūtaprakṛtipratyayādikalpanavad avidyāpade padārthakalpanāyāṃ tūkteṣu pakṣeṣu trayaḥ pakṣāḥ |
  yaś ca sambandho lakṣaṇāyā nimittaṃ taṃ pañcavidham āhuḥ | yathoktaṃ
  abhidheyena sambandhāt sādṛśyāt samavāyataḥ |
  vaiparītyāt kriyāyogāl lakṣaṇā pañcadhā matā || iti |
tatra dvirephādiśabdasya bhramarādiḥ śabdo 'bhidheyaḥ | tatsambandhāt tena ṣaṭpado lakṣyate iti abhidheyasambandhanimittatā |
  sādṛśyād yathā siṃho māṇavaka iti | yathā vā --
children.translated_text:
The sentence itself is the expresser of the sentence-meaning. Just as phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) [are] in words, so words in sentences are meaningless [individually]. Therefore indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) simply does not exist [in this view]. Just as a horse, urged by a whip, has the cognition 'I am being driven by this [person] to run'—so too, by the force of <s>pratibhā</s> (intuitive flash), the apprehension from a qualified sentence [arises], and that itself is the sentence-meaning. Just as the postulation of stems, suffixes, etc. is [ultimately] unreal, so too the postulation of word-meanings in the sphere of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance of the true nature)—yet in the views already stated, there are [still] three positions.
And the relation that is the ground of indication (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>)—they declare it to be fivefold. As stated:
'From relation with the denoted meaning, from similarity, from inherent connection, from contrariety, and from association with an action—indication is considered to be of five kinds.'
Therein, the word '<s>dvirepha</s>' (two r-sounds) has 'bee-sound' (<s>bhramarādi</s>) as its denoted meaning; from the relation with that, the bee (<s>ṣaṭpada</s>) is indicated—this is indication grounded in relation with the denoted meaning.
From similarity, as in 'a lion, [this] boy' (<s>siṃho māṇavakaḥ</s>). Or as—

children.text: varṣe samasta evaikaḥ ślāghyaḥ ko 'py eṣa vāsaraḥ |
children.translated_text: In the [whole] year, there is one single praiseworthy day, of some remarkable kind,

children.text: dinair mahattayānveyo yo na pūrvair na cāparaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: which is not equaled in its greatness by earlier or later days.

body.translated_text: In [the verse] beginning 'that man' (<s>sa puruṣaḥ</s>), the word '<s>puruṣa</s>' (man), being otherwise inapplicable [in its literal sense], has its expressible meaning (<s>vācya</s>) transferred to [an idea of] infinity through the suggested properties—such as 'possessing valor' and the like—that are indicated as belonging to it. Just as the word '<s>dvirepha</s>' (lit. 'two r-sounds') is used for the bee (<s>ṣaṭpada</s>) [because of its buzzing sound containing two 'r's], so [words like] '<s>dvika</s>' for the cuckoo (<s>kokila</s>) and so forth should not otherwise be employed.

body.text: atra prakaraṇavaśād mahāpuruṣaḥ kaścil lakṣyate yasya kule pūrve bhāvino vā puruṣā na samānatvam upayānti | samavāyaḥ uktasambandhebhyo 'nyaḥ sambandhaḥ | tato yathā [khaṇḍitaṃ pustakam atra] | sāmīpyād gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣa iti | sāhacaryāt chatriṇo yāntīti | atra hi chatrisāhacaryād achatrā apy evaṃ vyapadiśyante | vaiparītyād yathā kātare bhārgava iti | kriyāyogād yathā

children.text: pṛthur asi guṇaiḥ kīrtyā rāmo nalo bharato bhavān
children.translated_text: You are <s>Pṛthu</s> in virtues, <s>Rāma</s> in fame, <s>Nala</s> [and] <s>Bharata</s>—you are

children.text: mahati samara śatrughnas tvaṃ tathā janakaḥ sthiteḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Śatrughna</s> in great battle, and <s>Janaka</s> in steadfastness.
Thus bearing in your person the [merits of] ancient kings through your noble deeds,

children.text: katham asi na māṃdhātā deva trilokavijayy api ||
children.translated_text: how are you not [also] <s>Māndhātā</s>, O lord, conqueror of the three worlds?

body.translated_text: Here, by the force of context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), some great person (<s>mahāpuruṣa</s>) is indicated, whose ancestors or descendants do not attain equality [with him]. '<s>Samavāya</s>' (inherent connection) means a relation other than those already stated. From that, as in [a damaged manuscript passage here]. From proximity (<s>sāmīpya</s>), as in 'The village is on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>' (<s>gaṅgāyāṃ ghoṣaḥ</s>). From association (<s>sāhācarya</s>), as in 'The umbrella-bearers are going' (<s>chatriṇo yānti</s>)—here, by association with umbrella-bearers, even those without umbrellas are so designated. From contrariety (<s>vaiparītya</s>), as in '[calling] the coward a <s>Bhārgava</s> [i.e., Paraśurāma].' From association with an action (<s>kriyāyoga</s>), as—

children.translated_text: [A meaning] that is connected with the operations of <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) and <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication), and is accompanied by [factors such as] the clarity of intelligence, purity, skill, context, and the like —
that suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya artha</s>), well-established, belongs to <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion). // 6 //

children.text: yathā saṃketena mukhyārthabādhāditritayena ca sahāyenābhidhāyako lakṣakaś ca yathā vā pakṣadharmānvayavyatirekasahagato vivakṣāyā anumāpakaḥ tathā pratibhānair malyavidagdhaparicayaprakaraṇādijñānasāpekṣo vācako lakṣyakaś ca vyaṅgyam arthaṃ dhvaniśabdo vyanakti | tatra vyaṅgyaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as the denotative [function] and the indicative [function] operate with the aid of convention, obstruction of primary meaning, and the triad [of conditions]; and just as the inferential [cognition] — accompanied by the presence of the inferential mark in the subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>), positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) — causes inference of the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>); so too, the denotative and indicative [functions], dependent upon knowledge of clarity of intelligence, purity, skillful acquaintance, context, and the like, manifest the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya artha</s>) — and the word <s>dhvani</s> denotes this [process]. Among these, the suggested meaning —
when manifested by a [single] word (<s>pada</s>), for example:
[Prakrit:] "O merchant, ivory — from where for us? And tiger-skins?
As long as the daughter-in-law with disheveled hair moves about in the house."

body.translated_text: Here, even though he is not [actually] <s>Śatrughna</s>, by association with the action of slaying enemies (<s>śatrughna</s> = enemy-slayer), the designation '<s>Śatrughna</s>' is applied.

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] "O merchant, ivory — from where for us? And tiger-skins?
As long as the daughter-in-law with disheveled hair moves about in the house."
When manifested by a sentence (<s>vākya</s>), for example:

children.text: attā ettha ṇimajjai ettha ahaṃ diasaaḥ paloehi |
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] "The mother-in-law sinks [into sleep] here; here am I — look by daylight!

children.text: mā pahia rattiandhaa sejjāe maha ṇimajjahisi ||
children.translated_text: O traveler, blind in the dark of night, do not stumble upon one of our beds!"
[Sanskrit rendering:] "The mother-in-law sinks [into sleep] here; here am I — look by daylight!

children.text: mā pathika rātryandha śayyāyām āvayor nimaṅkṣyasi || ]
children.translated_text: O traveler, blind in the dark of night, do not stumble upon one of our beds!"

body.text:
atrābhidhānamūlaṃ vyañjanam | lakṣaṇāmūlaṃ yathā -- niśvāsāndha ivādarśa ity udāhṛtam |
sa eva guṇabhūtaḥ padaprakāśyo yathā --

children.translated_text: "The contriver of the gambling fraud, the igniter of the house of lac, that arrogant one,
skilled at removing <s>Kṛṣṇā's</s> (<s>Draupadī's</s>) upper garment — the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> are whose slaves;
the king, the master of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> and the rest, the elder brother of a hundred younger brothers, the friend of <s>Aṅgarāja</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>) —

children.text: kvāste duryodhano 'sau kathayata na ruṣā draṣṭum abhyāgatau svaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where is that <s>Duryodhana</s>? Tell him: not with anger, [but] we have come to see [him]."

body.translated_text: Here the suggestion is rooted in <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation). An example rooted in <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) is the one already cited: "Like a mirror clouded by breath." That same [suggested meaning], when subordinate (<s>guṇabhūta</s>), manifested by a word, is illustrated as follows:

body.text: atraite varākā dāsabhāvaṃ gatāḥ kiṃ kariṣyanti asmadekaśaraṇāḥ paribhaviṣyanti ityādi dyūtakāle bhavadbhiś cintitam āsīn nāsmakaṃ vismṛtam | tatra kācit pratikriyā nirvyūḍhā na kiṃ nirvyūḍhā ityādikaṃ tam artham abhivyajya sarvair eva kartā dyūtachalānām ityādibhir vācya evārthe viśramyate |

children.translated_text: When manifested by a sentence, [and subordinate], for example:
[Prakrit:] "Hearing the clamor of birds flying up from the thickets of reeds,
the limbs of the bride engaged in household work grow faint."

body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here [the suggested meaning is:] "These wretches have become slaves — what can they do? They have no refuge but us; they will be humiliated" — such was thought by you at the time of the gambling. Has it not been forgotten by us. Has some remedy been carried out [by you] for that, or has it not? — having suggested this meaning through all [the descriptions], the [speaker] comes to rest on the denotative meaning itself through "the contriver of the gambling fraud" and the other [phrases].

children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] "Hearing the clamor of birds flying up from the thickets of reeds,
the limbs of the bride engaged in household work grow faint."

body.text:
atra dattasaṃketaḥ puruṣo vānīralatāgṛhaṃ praviṣṭa iti vyaṅgyam artham avagamayya vācyo 'rthaḥ svaprādhānyenāsti | na caivam abhidhāyā lakṣaṇāyā vā kaścid avasara iti bhinnam eva dhvananam |
  nanu ‘yat paraḥ śabdaḥ sa śabdārtha'; iti vyaṅgyābhimato 'pi tātparyāt katham na vācyaḥ | iha sarvāṇy eva kārakāṇi kārakatvāt savyāpārāṇīti sādhyāyamānāny ato bhūtabhavyasamuccāraṇe "bhūtaṃ bhavyāyopadiśyata" ity adagdhadahananyāyena yāvad avahitaṃ tāvad vidhīyate iti kvacit kārakapadārtho 'pi viṣayo bhavati | yathā dadhnā juhoti payasā juhotīti | evaṃ hi pūrvo dhāvatīty aparārthe 'pi tātparyaṃ syāt | anvitaḥ padārtho 'bhihitānvaye anvitamātraṃ tv anvitābhidhāne | tatraiva saṃketopapatteḥ | anvitaviśeṣas tūbhayamate 'py avācya eva | evaṃ ca vācyatve kā vārttā vācyaviparītātmano vyaṅgyasya | na tu vyaṅgyam anumeyam iti śakyaṃ vaktum | na hi vācyavyaṅgyayoḥ pratibandhagrahe kiñcit pramāṇaṃ kramate | prakaraṇādisāmagrīm antareṇa hi na vyaṅgyam | na ca sā pramāṇagocarā | vyaṅgyavācināṃ tv adoṣaḥ | evaṃbhūtāyāṃ pramāṇair apratipannāyāṃ hi sāmagryām upapattim anapekṣyāpi samudayamānā pratītiḥ kena nihnotuṃ śakyata iti | siddham abhidhātātparyalakṣaṇāvyāpārātiriktaṃ dhvananam | etac cānyatra vistareṇa vicāritam iti saṃkṣepeṇehoktam iti śivam ||
body.translated_text: Here, having comprehended the suggested meaning — that the man with whom a tryst was arranged has entered the bower of reed-vines — the denotative meaning exists with its own predominance. Nor is there any occasion here for [the operation of] <s>abhidhā</s> or <s>lakṣaṇā</s> [to account for the suggestion]; hence <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) is indeed a distinct [word-function]. [Objection:] Now, [according to the maxim] "what comes after is the meaning of a word" — the meaning intended as suggested could also be the denoted meaning (<s>vācya</s>) through <s>tātparya</s> (purport). [Reply:] Here, since all <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations), being case-relations, are established as having functions — therefore, in the joint mention of past and future, "the past is taught for the sake of the future" — by the maxim of unburnt fire, [the injunction] extends as far as it is applicable; thus sometimes even the meaning of a case-word becomes the subject [of the injunction]. As in "he offers with curds, he offers with milk." For in the same way, "the former runs" would have purport also in the latter meaning. The connected word-meaning is [what is denoted] in the <s>abhihitānvaya</s> (expressed-connection) view; mere connection is [what is denoted] in the <s>anvitābhidhāna</s> (connection-expression) view — since convention is possible only there. But the specific connection is unexpressed (<s>avācya</s>) even in both views. And thus, when such is the case regarding the expressible, what need to speak of the suggested meaning which is of a nature opposite to the expressed? Nor can it be said that the suggested is merely inferred; for no valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) operates in grasping the invariable relation between the expressed and the suggested. Without the aggregate of context and other factors, there is no suggested meaning; and that aggregate is not the object of any [formal] means of knowledge. But for those who speak of suggested meaning, there is no fault; for when the aggregate is such — not established by formal means of knowledge — by what can the cognition that arises, even without depending on logical reasoning, be suppressed? Thus it is established that <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) is a word-function distinct from the operations of <s>abhidhā</s>, <s>tātparya</s>, and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>. This has been examined in detail elsewhere; hence it is stated here only in brief. May there be auspiciousness.
Thus concludes the <s>Śabdavyāpāravicāra</s> (Investigation of the Functions of Words) composed by the emperor among all scholars, the revered <s>Rājānaka Mammaṭācārya</s>.
